title: Lightweight lit-sprint: long-tail benchmarks + sketches
body:
Quick sprint notes — lightweight reading + action items.

Context: carving a 2-week rapid read+proto to evaluate long-tail prompt behavior under low-bit quantization and prefix/KV compression. Goal is a small, reproducible suite we can run on Redwood Dedicated to get cost/latency delta numbers.

Papers / posts skimmed (very terse takeaways):
1) "Efficient Prefix Compression for KV Caches" (arXiv 2029) — idea: compress contiguous prefix entries with a small transform (sparse factorization) so cache lookups remain O(1) but storage drops 3–4x. Observed tradeoff: slight decode latency ~2–6ms per request but big memory win when context windows are >64k tokens. Practical note: good fit for bursts of long sessions; not great for tiny RLHF-style episodes.
2) "Long-Tail Benchmarking for Language Models" (ICML 2029 workshop) — collection of prompts emphasizing rare entities, multi-hop retrieval, and length-conditioned failure modes. Has a small eval harness (python) with seed corpora. Useful as a superset for our lightweight bench.
3) "Quantization Degradation Patterns" (blog post, infra team) — qualitative: degradation isn't uniform across layers; attention heads near the end are more sensitive. Suggests hybrid quantization (mix 8-bit for attention proj, 4-bit for feedforward) yields best cost/quality trade.
4) "KV Eviction Heuristics Revisited" (short note) — simple LRW (length-weighted recency) beats pure LRU for dialog sessions with topic shifts.

Conference takeaways (ICML satellite chat notes):
- People care about deterministic fallbacks (if low-bit variant fails a QA pass, auto-fallback to 8-bit model for that query).
- Benchmarks trending toward operational reproducibility: small harness + seed corpus + deterministic randomness.
- There is appetite for a "long-window cost metric" (tokens-per-second-per-dollar at window==X). Could be a Redwood public benchmark.

Idea: build a 3-tier lightweight bench (sprint scope):
- Tier A: fidelity checks (small, 100 prompts from long-tail set) -> automated quality delta (EM / F1 / BLEU-ish depending).
- Tier B: throughput sweep (vary batch sizes, seq len, KV compression on/off) -> latency and memory footprint traces.
- Tier C: degradation probes (perturb input with OOV entities, change context order) -> robustness flags.

Planned proto tasks (actionable):
- [ ] Grab ICML long-tail corpus and pare down to 120 seed prompts (Antonia).
- [ ] Implement micro-harness that runs model variants (fp16, 8bit, 4bit hybrid) and records latency, mem, and quality (Eli).
- [ ] Wire a KV-compressed shim (Lina) that can toggle compression on a per-request basis and return decode penalty metric.
- [ ] Run initial sweep on a single p3-equivalent Dedicated node (cost-estimates in doc below).

Quick notes on measurement and pitfalls:
- Use deterministic seeds to compute exact EM diffs; ensemble randomness obscures small deltas.
- Warm cache vs cold cache matters a ton for long-window workloads — capture both.
- Measure per-token and end-to-end latency separately; sometimes decode penalty is amortized across very long outputs.
- Watch for tokenizer boundary effects when compressing KV prefixes (we saw off-by-one token mismatches in prior experiments).

Draft budget/estimate (rough):
- Setup (dev work for harness + KV shim): ~8 dev-days.
- Runs: 3 configs x 4 seq-len buckets x 10 seeds x small throughput sweep => ~72 runs. On one Dedicated node this is ~6–8 hours, $X (placeholder).

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is the KV compression approach compatible with our fallback routing? i.e., can we route to a decompressed variant cheaply?
- How to pick quality thresholds for auto-fallback without creating oscillation? Maybe use a conservative hysteresis window.
- Should we expose a public metric (tokens/$ at window N) or keep internal? Could be good marketing for Dedicated.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Finish seed selection (Antonia) and post to Slack channel #bench-small.
- Eli to prototype harness skeleton (pytest + small docker image).
- Lina to sketch API for compression toggle and estimate decode penalty via microbench.

Notes-to-self / heuristics collected:
- Prefer per-request tags for config (so we can replay exact scenario).
- Keep probe prompts small clusters (3–5) to test stateful eviction quickly.
- Log KV cache sizes as tokens + compressed-bytes.

References / bookmarks:
- arXiv:2901.01234 (Efficient Prefix Compression)
- ICML workshop page: long-tail-bench-2029
- Infra blog: Quantization Degradation Patterns (internal link)

End. More detailed writeup if the proto shows signal.

-- Antonia
